html:
The Huu-ay-aht are a Nuu-chah-nulth First Nation on the west coast of Vancouver Island, at Pachena Bay and along the Sarita River near Barkley Sound.

Like other Nuu-chah-nulth peoples they fished, gathered shellfish and hunted whales from dugout canoes. Huu-ay-aht oral history tells of a night when the sea destroyed the village at Pachena Bay; scientists link it to the Cascadia earthquake of 1700, whose tsunami also reached Japan.

They are neighbours of the Ditidaht and Tseshaht. The Huu-ay-aht signed the Maa-nulth Treaty with Canada and British Columbia, which took effect in 2011 and gave them self-government over their own lands.
sum: The Huu-ay-aht are a Nuu-chah-nulth First Nation on the west coast of Vancouver Island, at Pachena Bay and along the Sarita River near Barkley Sound.
